title: Psalms Chapter 144 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 144 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 144 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 144.

questions.question: Who is described as the strength that teaches hands to war and fingers to fight?
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:1 states that the LORD is the strength who teaches hands to war and fingers to fight.

questions.question: In Psalms 144, which of the following is NOT a description given for the LORD in verse 2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:2 describes the LORD as goodness, fortress, high tower, deliverer, shield, and trusted one, but not as shepherd.

questions.question: According to Psalms 144:3, what question is asked about man?
options: What is man that the LORD takes knowledge of him?
Where does man go after death?
questions.correctAnswer: What is man that the LORD takes knowledge of him?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 asks, 'LORD, what is man, that thou takest knowledge of him?'

questions.question: According to Psalms 144:4, man's days are compared to what?
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:4 says that man's days are as a shadow that passeth away.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do to the mountains in Psalms 144:5?
options: Touch them so they shall smoke
questions.correctAnswer: Touch them so they shall smoke
questions.explanation: Verse 5 requests the LORD to bow the heavens and touch the mountains so they shall smoke.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 144:1 says that David taught his hands to war and his fingers to fight.
questions.explanation: It is the LORD who teaches hands to war and fingers to fight, as stated in Psalms 144:1.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 144 describes the LORD as a high tower and a deliverer.
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:2 calls the LORD a high tower and a deliverer among other titles.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 144:4, man is eternal and his days are everlasting.
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:4 says man is like vanity and his days are as a shadow that passeth away, not eternal.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 144:3 questions why the LORD considers man and the son of man.
questions.explanation: Verse 3 asks, 'LORD, what is man, that thou takest knowledge of him?' and also about the son of man.

questions.question: Which of the following does Psalms 144:1 say the LORD teaches?
options: Hands to war and fingers to fight
Feet to run and mouth to sing
Heart to love and soul to pray
Eyes to see and ears to hear
questions.correctAnswer: Hands to war and fingers to fight
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:1 states the LORD teaches hands to war and fingers to fight.

questions.question: What does Psalms 144:2 say the LORD subdues?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says the LORD subdueth my people under me.

questions.question: According to Psalms 144:5, what does the psalmist ask the LORD to bow?
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:5 says, 'Bow thy heavens, O LORD, and come down.'

questions.question: In Psalms 144, what comes first in the sequence of requests to the LORD?
options: Shoot out thine arrows and destroy them
Bow thy heavens and come down
Cast forth lightning and scatter them
questions.correctAnswer: Bow thy heavens and come down
questions.explanation: Verse 5 begins with 'Bow thy heavens, O LORD, and come down,' before other requests in verses 6 and 7.

questions.question: What does Psalms 144:4 compare man to?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 states, 'Man is like to vanity.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 144:3, who is made account of by the LORD?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 asks, 'or the son of man, that thou makest account of him.'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 144 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 144 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 144:6, what actions does the Psalmist ask God to perform against the enemies?
options: Cast forth lightning, scatter them, shoot out arrows, and destroy them
Send peace and blessings upon them
Raise a mighty army against them
questions.correctAnswer: Cast forth lightning, scatter them, shoot out arrows, and destroy them
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:6 directly states that the Psalmist asks God to 'Cast forth lightning, and scatter them: shoot out thine arrows, and destroy them,' demonstrating a plea for divine intervention against enemies.

questions.question: What does Psalms 144:7 request God to do in order to deliver the Psalmist?
options: Send thine hand from above; rid me, and deliver me out of great waters
Make my enemies fall into pits
Give me wisdom to defeat my foes
questions.correctAnswer: Send thine hand from above; rid me, and deliver me out of great waters
questions.explanation: In Psalms 144:7, the Psalmist asks God to 'Send thine hand from above; rid me, and deliver me out of great waters,' symbolizing a call for rescue from overwhelming danger, which aligns with the theme of divine protection.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 144:8, how are the enemies described in terms of their speech and actions?
options: Their mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood
They speak words of truth and act justly
They preach peace but act violently
questions.correctAnswer: Their mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:8 characterizes the enemies as deceitful, saying 'Whose mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood,' emphasizing their untrustworthy nature.

questions.question: What musical instruments does the Psalmist mention in Psalms 144:9 for singing praises to God?
options: A psaltery and an instrument of ten strings
questions.correctAnswer: A psaltery and an instrument of ten strings
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:9 states, 'upon a psaltery and an instrument of ten strings will I sing praises unto thee,' highlighting the Psalmist's intent to worship God with these specific stringed instruments.

questions.question: According to Psalms 144:10, who is the one that gives salvation to kings and delivers David from harm?
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:10 affirms that 'It is he that giveth salvation unto kings: who delivereth David his servant from the hurtful sword,' clearly attributing salvation and deliverance to God.

questions.question: How does Psalms 144:6-7 together illustrate God's power and willingness to protect His people?
options: By showing God casting lightning and sending His hand from above to rescue
By emphasizing human strength in battle
By encouraging reliance on political alliances
By promoting self-defense without divine aid
questions.correctAnswer: By showing God casting lightning and sending His hand from above to rescue
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 together depict God’s active role in protection: casting lightning to scatter enemies (v6) and sending His hand from above to deliver from overwhelming danger (v7), illustrating both power and willingness to save.

questions.question: What spiritual virtue does Psalms 144:9 highlight through the Psalmist's commitment to sing a new song to God?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 144:9, the Psalmist expresses intent to 'sing a new song unto thee, O God,' emphasizing the virtue of praise and worship as an expression of faith and gratitude.

questions.question: A believer feels overwhelmed by adversaries who deceive and speak falsely. Based on Psalms 144:7-8, what biblical truth can encourage them?
options: God will deliver and protect from those whose words and actions are false
They must rely solely on their own wisdom
Ignore the adversaries and avoid confrontation
questions.correctAnswer: God will deliver and protect from those whose words and actions are false
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 teach that God intervenes to deliver from 'strange children' whose 'mouth speaketh vanity,' encouraging trust in God's protection against deceitful enemies.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 144:10 teaches that kings receive their salvation from God, who also protects David from the sword.
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:10 clearly states that God gives salvation to kings and delivers David from the hurtful sword, confirming the truth of this statement.

questions.question: What does Psalms 144:8 suggest about the character of those who oppose the Psalmist?
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:8 describes the enemies as having mouths that 'speaketh vanity' and right hands 'of falsehood,' indicating their deceitful and untrustworthy character.

questions.question: How does Psalms 144:9-10 teach us about the relationship between worship and divine deliverance?
options: Worship through song acknowledges God’s power to save and deliver
Deliverance comes only through human effort, not worship
Worship must be silent to be effective
questions.correctAnswer: Worship through song acknowledges God’s power to save and deliver
questions.explanation: The Psalmist commits to singing praises (v9) recognizing God as the one who gives salvation and delivers (v10), linking worship with acknowledgement of God's protective power.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 144:6 encourages believers to ask God to scatter their enemies by casting lightning and shooting arrows.
questions.explanation: Verse 6 explicitly requests God to 'Cast forth lightning, and scatter them: shoot out thine arrows, and destroy them,' encouraging believers to seek God's active protection.

questions.question: What does Psalms 144:7-8 teach about the nature of prayer for deliverance?
options: Prayer acknowledges danger from deceitful enemies and asks for God's rescue
Prayer ignores the reality of enemies
Prayer demands immediate physical victory without faith
Prayer is only for personal comfort, not deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer acknowledges danger from deceitful enemies and asks for God's rescue
questions.explanation: These verses show a prayer that recognizes the threat from false-speaking enemies and asks God to send His hand to deliver from 'great waters' and deception, teaching trust and dependence on God.

questions.question: According to Psalms 144:9, what attitude should believers have when praising God?
options: Sing a new song with joy and fresh devotion
Only sing when circumstances are perfect
questions.correctAnswer: Sing a new song with joy and fresh devotion
questions.explanation: The Psalmist declares intent to 'sing a new song unto thee,' indicating an attitude of joyful, renewed praise rather than repetition without heart.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 144:8 describes the enemies’ right hand as a symbol of truth and justice.
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:8 explicitly says the enemies' right hand is 'a right hand of falsehood,' indicating deceit rather than truth or justice.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 144 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 144.

questions.question: According to Psalms 144:11, from whom does David ask to be delivered?
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:11 specifically uses the phrase 'strange children' to describe those from whom David seeks deliverance.

questions.question: In Psalms 144:12, how are the sons described?
options: As plants grown up in their youth
questions.correctAnswer: As plants grown up in their youth
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states that sons are like 'plants grown up in their youth,' symbolizing strength and vitality.

questions.question: What metaphor is used for daughters in Psalms 144:12?
options: Corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace
questions.correctAnswer: Corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace
questions.explanation: The daughters are compared to corner stones, which are polished, indicating beauty and strength in the structure of a palace.

questions.question: Psalms 144:13 mentions garners being full. What does 'garners' refer to in this context?
questions.explanation: Garners are storehouses for grain, indicating abundance and provision in the community.

questions.question: Which of the following blessings is NOT mentioned in Psalms 144:14?
options: No breaking in or going out
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:14 lists oxen strong to labour, security from breaking in or going out, and no complaining in the streets, but does not mention grapes.

questions.question: How does Psalms 144:15 describe a happy people?
options: Those whose God is the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Those whose God is the LORD
questions.explanation: The verse concludes that happiness belongs to people whose God is the LORD, highlighting spiritual blessing over material.

questions.question: The phrase 'whose mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood' in Psalms 144:11 symbolizes what?
questions.explanation: The phrase metaphorically describes the deceitful nature of the enemies from whom David seeks deliverance.

questions.question: What literary device is prominent in Psalms 144:12, where sons and daughters are described in contrasting yet complementary images?
questions.explanation: The verse uses parallelism, a common Hebrew poetic device, juxtaposing sons as plants and daughters as corner stones to emphasize growth and stability.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage similarly speaks of children being a blessing and compares daughters to cornerstones, resonating with Psalms 144:12?
questions.explanation: Psalm 127:3-5 also celebrates children as a heritage and blessing from the LORD, echoing the theme in Psalms 144:12.

questions.question: In Psalms 144:13, the phrase 'sheep may bring forth thousands and ten thousands in our streets' most likely symbolizes what?
options: Prosperity and increase in the community
Literal sheep grazing in the city
The abundance of enemies surrounding the city
questions.correctAnswer: Prosperity and increase in the community
questions.explanation: The imagery of prolific sheep symbolizes abundant blessings and prosperity within the community.

questions.question: The request in Psalms 144:11 to be delivered from 'the hand of strange children' is best understood in the cultural context of ancient Near Eastern conflicts as what?
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, 'strange children' typically refers to foreign or alien peoples who are hostile, consistent with the plea for divine deliverance.

questions.question: Which Hebrew word underlying Psalms 144:15's phrase 'happy' or 'blessed' is often used in the Old Testament to denote spiritual well-being and divine favor?
questions.explanation: 'Ashrei' (אַשְׁרֵי) is the Hebrew term translated as 'happy' or 'blessed' and frequently used to express spiritual prosperity and divine favor in Psalms and elsewhere.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 144:14 includes a prayer for social justice, specifically mentioning 'no complaining in our streets.'
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:14 explicitly includes 'that there be no complaining in our streets,' indicating a desire for social harmony and justice.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 144:13 focuses on military strength and conquest as the primary blessing for the people.
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:13 emphasizes agricultural abundance and prosperity, such as full garners and prolific sheep, not military conquest.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God as a protector and deliverer found in Psalms 144:10?
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 4:18 speaks of the Lord delivering from every evil work, paralleling the deliverance theme in Psalms 144:10 where God delivers David from the sword.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 144 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 144 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 144:1 declare about the LORD?
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:1 states, 'Blessed be the LORD my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight:' indicating that the LORD equips David for battle.

questions.question: In Psalms 144:2, which of the following is NOT mentioned as an attribute of God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:2 lists attributes such as 'my goodness,' 'my fortress,' and 'my shield,' but does not mention 'my judge.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 144:3, what question does David pose about humanity?
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:3 asks, 'LORD, what is man, that thou takest knowledge of him!' indicating David's wonder about human significance.

questions.question: What metaphor does Psalms 144:4 use to describe man's nature?
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:4 states, 'Man is like to vanity: his days are as a shadow that passeth away,' portraying the fleeting nature of human life.

questions.question: What does David ask the LORD to do in Psalms 144:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:5 expresses David's plea for divine intervention: 'Bow thy heavens, O LORD, and come down: touch the mountains, and they shall smoke.'

questions.question: In Psalms 144:7, from what does David seek deliverance?
options: The hand of his own people
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:7 states, 'Rid me, and deliver me out of great waters, from the hand of strange children,' indicating a plea for protection from foreign adversaries.

questions.question: What type of music does David intend to use to praise God in Psalms 144:9?
options: A psaltery and an instrument of ten strings
questions.correctAnswer: A psaltery and an instrument of ten strings
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:9 mentions, 'I will sing a new song unto thee, O God: upon a psaltery and an instrument of ten strings will I sing praises unto thee.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 144:10, who does God deliver?
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:10 states, 'It is he that giveth salvation unto kings,' showing that God's deliverance extends to those in authority.

questions.question: What does David desire for his sons in Psalms 144:12?
options: To be as plants grown up in their youth
questions.correctAnswer: To be as plants grown up in their youth
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:12 expresses a desire for his sons 'to be as plants grown up in their youth,' indicating a wish for their flourishing.

questions.question: What does Psalms 144:14 say about the state of the oxen?
options: They may be strong to labour
questions.correctAnswer: They may be strong to labour
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:14 states, 'That our oxen may be strong to labour,' which signifies a desire for strength and productivity in the community.

questions.question: In Psalms 144:15, who is declared happy?
options: The people whose God is the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The people whose God is the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:15 states, 'Happy is that people, whose God is the LORD,' emphasizing the blessedness of those who have the LORD as their God.

questions.question: What does Psalms 144:8 say about the speech of strange children?
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:8 states, 'Whose mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood,' indicating the deceitful nature of their words.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight can be drawn from Psalms 144:5-6 and Psalms 144:11 regarding God's sovereignty?
options: God does not concern Himself with humanity
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:5-6 and 11 reflect God's sovereignty and willingness to intervene, as David calls upon Him to act against his enemies and aid him.

questions.question: What does the combination of Psalms 144:10 and Psalms 144:15 reveal about the relationship between God and His people?
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:10 and 15 show that God's deliverance is tied to the happiness of His people, indicating a close relationship characterized by blessing.

questions.question: In light of Psalms 144:3 and Psalms 144:4, what does this chapter teach about the nature of humanity?
options: Humanity is created in God's image
questions.explanation: Psalms 144:3 and 4 highlight human frailty and transient nature, portraying humanity as 'like to vanity' and 'as a shadow that passeth away.'
